turns.doctor_question: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I came in because... I just keep getting stuck on this thing with my face. There's this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and my cheek. I notice it all the time in photos, and the bright lights at the store where I work make it seem so obvious. 

Other people tell me they don't even see it when I point it out, but... it just really feels like it's the very first thing customers and my managers notice when they look at me. It's just been bothering me a lot lately.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent preoccupation with a perceived uneven spot on their face that others state they cannot see, causing significant distress.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations, like social events or even work, because you're worried about how your face looks?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really avoid things. I mean, I still go to work every day and I still hang out with my friends. I don't like how it looks, especially under the store lights, but it doesn't stop me from doing what I need to do. I just... I think about it a lot while I'm there. But I don't stay home or anything like that.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient notes persistent concern regarding how their face looks, stating they dislike its appearance and think about it a lot even while at work and around others, confirming preoccupation with appearance.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to cover it up, because of how you feel about that area around your nose and cheek?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I guess I do. Um, when I'm on my breaks at work, I usually end up going to the bathroom just to check my face in the mirror. I'll try to fix my hair around it, just to see if it helps hide it. And... I also find myself comparing my face to the girls who come through my checkout line. Sometimes I actually take so long in the bathroom doing all that, I end up being late getting back to the register.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive appearance-related behaviors, specifically checking the bathroom mirror, camouflaging with hair, and comparing their face to customers.

turns.doctor_question: Does thinking about that uneven spot on your face ever make you feel very anxious, upset, or self-conscious to the point where it interferes with your focus or mood during the day?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it does. Like I was saying about taking too long in the bathroom... my manager has actually started to notice that I'm coming back from my breaks late. She also pointed out that I've been moving slower at the register, I guess because I just get so distracted thinking about my face while I'm ringing people up. It makes me really anxious because I'm actually trying to get a promotion right now, and I'm worried all of this is just making me look completely unreliable.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms that preoccupation with their facial appearance distracts them and causes anxiety and functional impairment at work.
